findings.title: CostWidget's headline dollar figure fabricates a truthful-looking $0.00 on a genuine fetch failure — a gap the in-flight spend-truth PR does not close
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/DashboardPage.tsx:257 `const costData = costQuery.isError ? null : costQuery.data?.data;` then line ~509 `totalCostUsd={costData?.total_cost_usd ?? 0}` with no isError/sourceError prop passed to CostWidget at all on current main (frontend/src/components/costs/CostWidget.tsx:24-54 has no error branch in its interface). PR #3461 (bu-kqnum.7, under review) adds a `sourceError` prop, but wires it as `costSourceError = costData?.source_error === true` (gh pr diff 3461, DashboardPage.tsx hunk) — computed from a field INSIDE `costData`, which is `null` whenever `costQuery.isError` is true. So even after #3461 merges, a plain network/5xx failure on GET /api/spend/summary (as opposed to a backend-reported degraded-envelope `source_error:true`) still drives `costSourceError` to `false` and renders a bare '$0.00' 'Cost Today' — indistinguishable from a real zero-spend day. Live-confirmed the endpoint currently returns a real payload with `meta:{}` (no source_error field yet): `curl http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/spend/summary?window=today` → `{"data":{...,"total_cost_usd":0.276289},"meta":{}}`.
findings.detail: This is a fabricated-data-with-real-data-authority instance distinct from the in-flight ledger-truth work (item 7 handles the backend's own placeholder-envelope compat field; it does not handle the frontend hook's own isError branch collapsing to null). The fix is one line: thread `costQuery.isError` (not just the backend's `source_error` field) into the same sourceError prop so any fetch failure — compat-envelope or hard network error — renders the same honest 'unavailable' treatment CostStripeChart already has on /spend.

findings.title: Board header/footer render a fabricated all-clear during a real board-fetch failure
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/ui/page.tsx:425-442 -- for archetype='status-board', on error!=null the Page shell still renders `<ArchetypeWrapper header={header} footer={footer}>` above the red error card (header/footer are NOT suppressed on error, unlike other archetypes). ButlersPage.tsx:107-111 passes `pageError = isError && !hasRows ? error : null` (full-page error path), but header/footer keep receiving `aggregates` from useButlerStatusBoard, whose every field is `agg?.X ?? <zero/false default>` when `boardQuery.data` is undefined (use-butler-status-board.ts:227-249). BoardHeader.tsx:44-49 `pillDotClass`: `if (total === 0) return 'bg-[var(--green)]'` -- so during the outage the pill renders a GREEN dot with aria-label '0 of 0 reporting healthy' and BoardFooter renders Active 0 / Offline 0 / Quarantined 0 / Spend $0.00 / Avg load -- with `costSourceError`/`sessionsSourceError` both false (they only flip on a per-field agg value, never on the top-level query failing), so none of BoardFooter's own SourceDegradedNote guards fire.
findings.failure_scenario: Board API/DB is down (the exact moment the owner most needs an honest signal): the page shows a red 'Something went wrong' card, but directly above it a green dot reads '0/0 reporting' and a calm KPI band reads Active 0, Offline 0, Spend $0.00 -- a screen reader announces '0 of 0 reporting healthy' verbatim. This is the failure-impersonating-calm sin at the top of the fleet-verification surface, worse than a blank page because it looks like a report, not an error.

Two adjacent widgets on the identical payload disagree about whether the fleet is healthy -- the exact 'three irreconcilable counts' sin recurring within a single component pair, not just across pages.

findings.title: Cadence label bucketing collapses any cadence up to 2 hours into 'hourly' -- live-confirmed mislabeling 5-minute crons
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/butlers.py:481-491 `_cadence_label`: `if cadence_seconds <= 3600*2: return 'hourly'`. Live GET /api/butlers/board (2026-07-22) returns chronicler/education/finance/general all with `cadence_seconds: 300.0` (i.e. a 5-minute cron interval per roster/chronicler/butler.toml:48-50 `cron = '*/15 * * * *'` and denser schedules) and `cadence_label: 'hourly'`. StatusBoardCell.tsx:90-100 `cadenceTooltip` and NeedsYouStrip.tsx:36-38 `reasonFor` both surface this label verbatim as 'silent Xd, expected hourly'.
findings.failure_scenario: A butler whose real cadence is every 5 minutes goes silent for 90 minutes; the owner reads 'silent 1h30m, expected hourly' and reasonably concludes it's within its normal cadence window -- when in fact it has missed roughly 18 consecutive scheduled runs. The bucketing function (built specifically to make cadence honest, per its own doctrine comment) actively launders a 24x understatement of overdue severity for any sub-2h schedule, which given the roster's *:15/*:30-minute schedules is most of the fleet.

findings.title: The board's 'refreshes every 30s' caption is a hardcoded constant, structurally decoupled from the real bus-aware interval it claims to describe, and never surfaces bus health
findings.evidence: ButlersPage.tsx:46 `const REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS = 30_000` is passed straight to BoardHeader as a literal caption ('refreshes every 30s') independent of the query's actual `refetchInterval`. use-butlers.ts:50-60 `useButlersBoard` sets `refetchInterval = useBusAwarePollInterval()`. use-bus-aware-poll-interval.ts:30-35 and lib/poll-policy.ts:23,43: when the event bus is 'open' (the healthy, common case) the real interval is `POLL_BUS_RECONCILE_MS = 5*60_000` (5 minutes); the 30s figure is only `POLL_BUS_DOWN_FALLBACK_MS`, the degraded-bus fallback. BoardHeader never calls `useEventBus()` to show bus status.
findings.failure_scenario: During normal healthy operation (bus connected) the board actually reconciles by poll only once every 5 minutes -- real-time freshness depends entirely on the websocket bus, which the header gives the owner zero visibility into. The caption always claims '30s' regardless, so the owner has no way to tell (a) the true worst-case staleness is 10x higher than displayed, or (b) whether the bus that provides the real-time updates is even connected right now.

findings.title: Sync staleness has no severity ladder: a source dead 114 days renders with the identical amber 'degraded' dot as one 6 minutes past threshold
findings.evidence: Live GET /api/calendar/workspace/meta (127.0.0.1:42200) returned a connected source ('Tze How NYC Surgery 2026', sync_enabled:true) with last_synced_at 2026-03-30T16:46:56Z, staleness_ms 9830542539 (~113.8 days) and sync_state 'stale'. Backend classification at src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:7966-7977 has only three outcomes — failed (explicit last_error), stale (staleness_ms > stale_threshold_ms, a small multiple of the sync interval, floor 5min), fresh — with no escalating tier by magnitude. Frontend syncDotState (CalendarWorkspacePage.tsx:1156-1163) maps sync_state 1:1 to StateDot severity: 'stale' always renders 'degraded' (amber), never 'error' (red), regardless of staleness_ms.
findings.detail: The freshness-plaque text is honest (formatFreshnessPlaqueDetail correctly renders '114 days ago', lines 364-384 — no fabrication), but the visual severity is flat: a source that has been dark for months looks exactly as alarming as one that missed a single sync cycle by a few minutes. An owner scanning the Sources rail for anything red-flagged would sail past a functionally-dead connector because its dot color matches a benign blip. This under-signals a real integrity risk (is the OAuth grant to this calendar even still valid?) and is a new instance of the 'staleness never wears current-data authority' principle being only half-implemented — text is truthful, but color/severity is not staleness-proportional.

audits.page: /chronicles (ChroniclesPage.tsx + roster/chronicler briefing pipeline)
audits.jarvis_gap: Chronicles is meant to be the owner's calm, trustworthy retrospective voice on their own day — the one place a busy owner reads instead of digging through raw episodes. Live verification shows the 'voice' column, the single thing the owner reads first, is not a narrated summary at all on stale-cache days: it is the LLM session's own planning monologue and tool-call trace, verbatim, including exactly the kind of machine-identifier text the day-close prompt explicitly forbids printing. Worse, the content is not even about the displayed day — a one-day content/date mismatch that breaks the signal->session->evidence trace spine at its first hop. And the page's own backward-navigation bound (earliest_date) is corrupted by an un-sanity-checked recurring calendar artifact, letting the stepper wander into 122 years of fabricated 'quiet' days that are indistinguishable from real monitored quiet days. A JARVIS-grade Chronicles never lets the owner read raw agent scaffolding as narrative, never presents a day it has no right to have an opinion about as 'quiet', and never lets a single bad row corrupt the archive's temporal shape.

findings.title: Editorial 'voice paragraph' is a raw LLM session dump, not narrated prose — violates the day-close prompt's own no-machine-identifiers rule
findings.evidence:
Live GET http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/chronicler/briefing?date=2026-07-21&tz=Asia/Singapore returns voice_paragraph = "I’ll use the reconciled day-close bundle for 2026-07-20 in Asia/Singapore, then send the single Telegram recap.
The reconciled bundle has activity to summarize... 

MCP tools called:

- `chronicler_day_close_bundle` — `date_label=2026-07-20`, `timezone=Asia/Singapore`
- `notify` — Telegram `send` with the day-close summary (deferred by delivery policy)". This is the agent's self-narration plan plus a literal tool-call/params trace, not the 3-10 bullet narrated summary the prompt demands. The day-close prompt itself (roster/chronicler/butler.toml lines ~190-210) explicitly forbids this: 'Does not print raw source_ref values, connector IDs, database keys, or other machine identifiers' and 'Does not mention bundle internals such as episodes_truncated... token-bounded'. `write_day_close_cache` persists `output.strip()` verbatim into `tier2_cache.prose` (src/butlers/chronicler/day_close_writer.py:210-219) with zero validation that the output is actually narrative prose vs. scaffolding/trace text, and `_voice_paragraph_from_cache` (roster/chronicler/api/router.py:2984-3023) reads it back unmodified for direct render as ChroniclesPage.tsx's `Elaboration` component (the page's own docstring at ChroniclesPage.tsx:15-17 claims this text 'obeys the voice rules... sentence case, no em-dashes' — the live content violates that too, with markdown bullets and backticked tool names).

findings.title: Displayed day and cached voice content are a full day apart — the trace spine breaks between selected date and its evidence
findings.evidence: The same live response is keyed to date=2026-07-21 (URL param, cache_key would be `day_close:2026-07-21` per _compute_day_window in src/butlers/chronicler/day_close_writer.py:126-150) but the cached prose's own text says `chronicler_day_close_bundle` was called with `date_label=2026-07-20` — i.e. the session that produced this cached paragraph summarized the wrong day, one day earlier than the key it was filed under. The frontend's only signal of anything being off is the generic 'stale' badge (ChroniclesPage.tsx:315-323, tooltip 'The day-close summary may be out of date') which reads as ordinary cache staleness, not 'this narrative describes an entirely different calendar day than the one you are viewing'. An owner reading yesterday's chronicle is reading a summary of the day before, with no way to discover that mismatch short of noticing the date_label buried in the dumped tool-call text (finding above).

findings.title: earliest_date archive bound is corrupted by an un-sanitized recurring-calendar artifact, letting the date stepper navigate into 122 years of fabricated 'quiet' days
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/chronicler/briefing?date=1950-06-15&tz=Asia/Singapore returns state_class='quiet', headline='Quiet day.', voice_paragraph='The day produced no projected episodes. Nothing needs attention.', and 7 recent_days rows all episode_count:0 — rendered identically to a genuine monitored quiet day (STATE_PREDICATE.quiet composes to '<subject> was quiet.' in ChroniclesPage.tsx:56-66, with no distinction for a pre-data/nonexistent day). This is reachable because `earliest_date` (the backward navigation clamp, ChroniclesPage.tsx:161-186, isAtEarliest/clampIsoDay in chronicles-date-nav) is computed as raw `MIN(start_at)` over ALL non-tombstoned episodes with no floor (src/butlers/chronicler/editorial.py:524-541, `_fetch_earliest_episode_date`). Live: GET /api/chronicler/episodes?start_from=1904-01-01T00:00:00Z&start_to=1905-01-01T00:00:00Z returns exactly one row: a `google_calendar.completed` recurring-birthday instance ('Hui Min Lee\'s birthday', category=other) anchored at 1904-10-18T00:00:00Z — a classic no-year-set Google recurring-event artifact, not real chronicled activity. That single row sets the whole archive's earliest_date to 1904-10-18, so the '[' previous-day stepper and command-palette 'Previous day' action (ChroniclesPage.tsx:196-204, 237-243) can walk the owner across 122 years of days the system could not possibly have any evidence about, each one rendered with full 'quiet, nothing to see' calm authority identical to a real monitored day.

findings.title: Closed decision bead still rendered as 'waiting' due to export-mirror staleness, with no per-row stale-data tell
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/decisions (12:24 UTC) lists bu-kqnum.9.6.3 as an open decision, age_hours=12.0, with meta.export_as_of=2026-07-22T02:20:10Z. `bd show bu-kqnum.9.6.3 --json` shows status=closed, closed_at=2026-07-22T05:24:56Z (merged PR #3501, per commit 8ff1648d). The export snapshot backing the API was taken ~3h before the bead closed and the API is still serving it ~7h after close. decision_review.py's `_is_decision_bead` (lines 233-258) correctly filters `_OPEN_STATUSES` -- the bug is not the filter, it's that the single-file bind-mount (docstring lines 17-56) can lag bd's live state by hours, and DecisionsPage.tsx has no per-row staleness indicator -- only a page-level 'export as of Xh ago' plaque that stays muted until 48h (_EXPORT_AS_OF_WARN_HOURS, DecisionsPage.tsx:68), well past the window in which this false-positive is visible.
findings.detail: A decision the owner already resolved (or that closed itself via automation) continues to read as 'N decisions waiting' with no warning that it may already be moot -- this is the exact 'staleness never wears current-data authority' violation the vision names, occurring at normal operating cadence (hours), not just the 14-day export_missing/export_stale cliff the code explicitly guards against. The owner acting on this list wastes attention re-deciding something already closed, and the escalation/verdict-opener counts ('4 decisions waiting') are inflated by ghosts.

findings.title: Sidebar 'Decisions' badge collapses export-unavailable to a bare 0, indistinguishable from a genuine all-clear
findings.evidence: frontend/src/hooks/use-qa-badge.ts:41-51, `useDecisionsOpenBadge`: `if (!data || data.meta?.decisions_available === false) return 0` -- its own docstring admits 'the badge has no "unavailable" affordance, unlike the /decisions page's own verdict opener, which does surface that flag loudly.' nav-config.ts:75 wires this into the persistent sidebar badge (amber variant) that renders on every page, not just /decisions.

This is a new, concrete instance of 'errors impersonating calm empty states' that the page itself already guards against but the badge upstream of it does not.

findings.title: The shipped decision-bead structured convention (bu-ckkpz.1) has zero live adoption and no compliance signal reaches the owner or the digest
findings.evidence: Live: `python3 scripts/lint_decision_beads.py --json` against the current queue reports both open decision beads (bu-kqnum.10.5, bu-kqnum.3.3) failing all four checks: missing metadata.decision.options, missing metadata.decision.default, missing due_at. Source: decision_review.py's weekly digest only calls `_run_unlabeled_marker_lint` (line 693) which runs the lint script in `--check-unlabeled-markers` mode -- that mode only widens discovery to catch title-marker beads missing the `decision` label; it does not surface structured-field violations on beads that already carry the label (confirmed by reading lint_decision_beads.py's `--check-unlabeled-markers` docstring, lines 39-58). Additionally, `grep -n metadata` decision_review.py returns zero hits: the digest computation (`DecisionBead` dataclass, lines 161-168, and its builder) never reads `metadata.decision` or `due_at` at all, even for a hypothetically-compliant bead.
findings.detail: bu-ckkpz.3 (attention-ledger routing + Telegram one-tap close) is documented as blocked purely on bu-24lu6.4/.5's inline-keyboard primitives, but this audit shows a second, deeper gap: even once unblocked, there is no wired data path from a bead's actual options/default to the digest or UI, AND real bead authors (including the fleet itself, minting bu-kqnum.10.5/.3.3 this week) are not using the structured fields the convention mandates -- with no lint or digest signal telling anyone. The convention is de facto decorative: a linter exists, but nothing runs it against compliant discovery scope or surfaces its findings, so drift is permanent and invisible.

findings.title: Decision rows are a drill-down dead end: no description/options ever reach the API or page, and no deep link to the underlying bead exists anywhere in the dashboard
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/decisions omits `description` for every row -- e.g. bu-kqnum.3.3's real content (a numbered list of six concrete decision options, verified via `bd show bu-kqnum.3.3 --json`) never appears in the API payload or DecisionsPage.tsx's DecisionRow detail panel (lines 144-169), which explicitly states 'No actions are available in this read-only digest... options and close controls are not included here.' `grep -rln 'bd show\|beads.dev\|/beads/' frontend/src/pages/*.tsx` returns zero matches across the whole dashboard -- there is no bead-deep-link affordance anywhere to hop from a dashboard row to the bead's full content in bd or GitHub.
findings.detail: This directly breaks 'every clause a door on an unbroken trace spine (signal -> session -> evidence)': the Decisions page's door opens onto a title and an age, then dead-ends -- the owner must already know to leave the dashboard entirely and run `bd show <id>` in a terminal to read what they're actually being asked to decide. For a page whose entire purpose is surfacing decisions the owner must act on, this is the single largest usability gap: verification (page 1) works, but action-readiness (the actual decision content) is unreachable from the UI.

audits.ideal: The ideal /decisions is a live, self-healing decision desk: the sidebar badge and the page's verdict opener share one honest source-of-truth vocabulary (open / N waiting / degraded -- never a bare 0 standing in for 'unknown'), the underlying beads-export bind-mount is refreshed fast enough (or reconciled defensively) that a bead closed minutes ago cannot still read as 'waiting' with no tell, and every decision-labeled bead is authored with real structured options/default/due_at (enforced at creation time, not just linted after the fact) so the digest can render the actual choice inline -- default highlighted, deadline countdown visible, one tap (Telegram or dashboard) commits the choice and closes the loop through the attention ledger. Each row is a door two hops deep at most: select to see full context (description, options, blocked dependents), one keystroke to act or one click to jump to the canonical bead/PR for anything the digest doesn't carry. Nothing here is a summary of a summary -- the page shows exactly what bd knows, as fresh as bd knows it, and says so the moment it doesn't.
audits.jarvis_gap: The page is an honest, well-built read-only mirror of a digest that is itself hollow: it faithfully renders what decision_review.py computes, but that computation (a) can lag live bd state by hours with no per-row tell, (b) never reads the structured options/default/due_at fields the convention mandates -- fields that, live-checked, no real decision bead currently populates anyway -- and (c) carries no description at all, so the page cannot show the owner what they're actually deciding. The gap is not in the page's honesty machinery (degraded notes, verdict opener, staleness plaque are all solid); it's that the desk has nothing to act on yet, and the fleet has no feedback loop telling it that the convention it shipped isn't being used.

audits.jarvis_gap: Education renders as a fully-built adaptive-learning dashboard (mind-map graph, mastery analytics, review timeline, quiz history) but the one live curriculum in the system has been a zero-node, zero-flow phantom for 31 days, invisible to every lifecycle job that could catch and fix it, while the UI narrates it as a normal in-progress build. A JARVIS-grade surface would guarantee that 'active' means 'owned by a live process' -- every mind_map row is created transactionally with its teaching_flow record (or not created at all), a visible SLA/staleness clock replaces the evergreen 'still building it' copy once a map exceeds the expected build time, review-timeline entries and analytics struggling-nodes are first-class drill-down entries into the same node-detail panel regardless of which tab you're on, and the backend's own /flows endpoint (with real per-flow state, session_count, mastery_pct) is the frontend's primary curriculum-health view instead of being invisible to it.

findings.title: Orphaned mind map bypasses the teaching_flow state machine entirely -- invisible to /flows, invisible to the stale-flow cleanup job, permanently 'active' with zero nodes for 31+ days
findings.evidence: Live: GET /api/education/mind-maps returns d3758b20-6816-43b3-845c-0e9e0405cb82 ("Systems Programming - SPSC & CPU Pinning", status=active, created_at 2026-06-21, root_node_id=null, nodes=[], edges=[]) -- 31 days old as of 2026-07-22, still zero nodes; GET .../analytics returns 404 'No analytics snapshot found'; GET .../frontier returns []. Live: GET /api/education/flows (unfiltered) returns only one entry, the unrelated __probe_not_used__/abandoned map -- d3758b20 does not appear at all. Source: roster/education/tools/teaching_flows.py:562-573 `teaching_flow_list` calls `state_get(pool, _flow_key(map_id))` per mind_map row and does `if flow_state is None: continue` -- proving no flow-state KV entry was ever written for d3758b20. The dashboard's own `weekly-stale-flow-check` schedule (roster/education/butler.toml) and `check_stale_flows` operate over teaching_flow_list, so a mind_map with no flow record can never be auto-abandoned or nudged.
findings.failure_scenario: The dashboard's curriculum-request flow (roster/education/api/router.py:641-674, `_drain_prompt`) delegates the mind_map->flow linkage to an LLM session's natural-language obedience: the prompt instructs the session to call `teaching_flow_start(...)` (step 2) then `state_delete(pending_curriculum_request)` (step 4), but nothing enforces step 2 actually ran via `teaching_flow_start` rather than a bare mind_map_create/curriculum_generate call, and nothing re-attaches a flow record after the fact. Once such a gap occurs the resulting mind_map is a permanent zombie: selectable in the dropdown, polled every 30s, rendered with 'This curriculum has no concepts yet. The butler is still building it.' (MindMapGraph.tsx:160-165) with no distinguishing signal between 'requested 30 seconds ago' and 'dead for a month'.

moves.title: Make mind_map creation and teaching_flow attachment one atomic operation; kill the LLM-obedience-only lock release

findings.title: Merging your currently-viewed entity away leaves you stranded on its own tombstone with zero indication it was merged
findings.evidence: Live-confirmed: GET http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/memory/entities/c37e8577-ce84-4ed2-a638-4e6346afd0c2 (a real tombstoned entity found via `SELECT id, canonical_name, metadata->>'merged_into' FROM public.entities WHERE metadata ? 'merged_into'`) returns HTTP 200 with `fact_count: 0`, `recent_facts: []`, `dunbar_tier: null`, and `metadata.merged_into: '7c1eadf3-...'` buried in the payload. frontend/src/pages/EntityDetailPage.tsx never reads `entity.metadata.merged_into` (grep confirms zero references) and src/butlers/api/routers/memory.py:1542-1553 `get_entity()` has no `merged_into IS NULL` guard (unlike every list/index query, e.g. src/butlers/modules/contacts/backfill.py:170, src/butlers/api/read_models/search_v1.py:289, which all filter it). Mechanism: useMergeRelationshipEntities (frontend/src/hooks/use-entities.ts:637-654) invalidates BOTH `["memory-entity", entityA]` and `["memory-entity", entityB]` after a merge, and EntityDetailPage.tsx:3188 renders `<MergeCompareDialog pair={comparePair} .../>` with no `onResolved` prop (contrast: EntitiesIndexPage.tsx:1609 passes `onResolved={() => setSelectedIds(new Set())}`). So a user who opens the merge-review from the `m` key or the Workbench duplicate panel while viewing entity A, then keeps B as survivor, has their own open tab silently refetch A's now-emptied record in place — no redirect to the survivor, no banner, and every curation button (Merge/Promote/Demote/Archive/Forget/Edit aliases) stays fully enabled on the zombie record.
findings.detail: This is the calm-empty-state sin at the object-identity level, not the query-result level: staleness (a tombstoned record) wears the full authority of a genuinely quiet, low-activity contact. The information needed to prevent it (`metadata.merged_into`) is already being returned by the API — this is a pure frontend gap, one `if (entity.metadata?.merged_into) redirect/banner` away from being fixed, with the target id already in hand for a same-page redirect.

findings.title: Merge fires immediately with no confirmation step, while the objectively-lesser-scope Forget requires a two-step AlertDialog
findings.evidence: source-confirmed: MergeCompareDialog.tsx:280-292 `handleMerge()` calls `merge.mutateAsync(...)` directly off the `data-testid="compare-merge"` button (MergeCompareDialog.tsx:385-397) — no window.confirm, no AlertDialog. Compare EntityDetailPage.tsx:3145-3185, where Forget requires opening an `<AlertDialog>` (`forgetDialogOpen`) with a distinct 'Forget this entity?' title and a second explicit click on AlertDialogAction before `handleForgetConfirm()` runs. Grepping the whole codebase (`grep -rn "unmerge\|un-merge\|reverse.*merge" src/butlers`) turns up no un-merge/reverse-merge capability anywhere — src/butlers/modules/memory/tools/entities.py:1211 `entity_merge()` repoints facts, unions aliases/roles, and tombstones the source with no code path back. Merge is therefore at least as irreversible as Forget (arguably more so — it commingles two identity records' full fact history) yet has strictly less friction: one radio-select + one click vs. Forget's two clicks across two distinct UI surfaces.
findings.detail: Design-bar Recovery principle: 'require explicit confirmation where the action is not reversible.' The compare dialog is a review step, not a confirm step — reviewing the diff and clicking 'Merge' in the same gesture is exactly the pattern the bar calls out as insufficient for an irreversible action.

audits.ideal: The ideal entity dossier treats identity as a first-class, provably-alive concept, not just a UUID that happens to resolve. On open, the detail page's very first check is liveness: if `metadata.merged_into` is present, the page never renders the normal dossier at all — it immediately shows a small "merged into {survivor name} on {date}" redirect card with a one-click jump to the survivor (the survivor id and name are already in the payload; zero extra fetches needed), and every curation action is absent, not just disabled, because there is nothing left to curate. Merging itself becomes a single unbroken transaction from the user's point of view: review the diff, pick the survivor, confirm irreversibility explicitly (a short typed-or-clicked second step matching Forget's ceremony, since merge is at least as destructive), and on success the app navigates you to the survivor's page with a toast that is also a link — you're never left staring at a record that no longer conceptually exists. The dossier and the merge/dedup flow together read as one continuous spine: opening any entity, spotting a duplicate signal, reviewing evidence, committing (or dismissing) a decision, and landing on solid ground afterward — never a gap where the UI still trusts a UUID the backend has already retired.
audits.jarvis_gap: The five-second fleet-verification promise breaks specifically at the moment of highest stakes on this surface: right after the owner corrects the graph by merging a duplicate. Instead of confirming the correction landed, the page can silently keep showing the pre-merge record as if nothing happened — indistinguishable from a legitimately quiet, sparse contact. Earned calm requires that staleness never wear current-data authority; a tombstoned identity record is the most literal form of staleness this surface can produce, and it currently wears full authority with zero markers.

findings.title: Reauth CTA hard-navigates to a raw JSON 404 for any non-OAuth-registry connector type (WhatsApp confirmed)
findings.evidence: frontend/src/pages/ConnectorDetailPage.tsx:163-180 handleReauth derives `provider = connectorType.startsWith('google') ? 'google' : connectorType` (so whatsapp_user_client -> provider='whatsapp_user_client', not the catalog id 'whatsapp'), builds a URL via getProviderOAuthStartUrl (frontend/src/api/client.ts:3650), and does `window.location.href = url` -- a full-page browser navigation, not a fetch. Backend src/butlers/api/routers/oauth.py:2698-2730: `_get_provider_config('whatsapp_user_client')` returns None; `_is_catalog_oauth_provider` checks `PROVIDER_CATALOG.get(provider)` keyed on the real catalog id 'whatsapp' (src/butlers/secrets_provider_catalog.py:83) -- 'whatsapp_user_client' isn't in the catalog either, so the request falls through to the `unknown_provider` 404 JSON branch (line 2723-2730), not even the friendlier 501 'oauth_provider_not_configured' path. ReauthCallout (frontend/src/components/ingestion/connectors/ReauthCallout.tsx) and connector-auth.ts's deriveConnectorDispatchInfo never special-case connector type -- any connector in `state==='error'` gets the same generic 'reauth required' CTA. The real WhatsApp relink mechanism (QR pairing via POST /api/connectors/whatsapp/pair/start, frontend/src/hooks/use-whatsapp.ts) lives entirely on the Secrets passport page and is never linked from here.
findings.failure_scenario: WhatsApp session logs out (state='error') -> connector detail page shows the standard red 'reauth required' banner with a re-authorize button (identical treatment to Google/Spotify) -> operator clicks it, expecting the usual OAuth redirect -> browser navigates away from the dashboard entirely to a bare `{"error":"unknown_provider","provider":"whatsapp_user_client",...}` JSON page, with no toast, no back-link, no indication the real fix (QR pairing in Secrets) even exists. Operator must know to abandon this flow, hit browser back, and independently discover the Secrets passport path.

audits.page: /issues + /audit-log (IssuesPage.tsx, AuditLogPage.tsx, api/routers/audit.py, api/routers/issues.py)
audits.jarvis_gap: Issues is close to the JARVIS bar (URL-backed filters, honest degraded-source envelope, occurrence drill-down, j/k+ack triage, command palette). Audit Log — the evidentiary backstop every Issues row ultimately drills into — is architecturally behind: it never adopted the fleet's keyset-pagination convention, its default (safest) 'Privileged' view is live-measured 3-6x SLOWER than the noisy unfiltered view because the consequence-allowlist predicate has no supporting index and forces a parallel sequential scan of a continuously-growing 1.38M-row table, deep pagination degrades linearly with no jump-to-date/page escape hatch, and it has zero keyboard/command-palette surface despite being a hot investigative loop. The ideal surface: audit-log is the terminal evidence tier of the trace spine, so it must be as fast on page 200 as page 1, filterable at the same URL-shareable fidelity as Issues, keyboard-navigable row-by-row with an 'open in Issues' door already in view, and its default filter must be the cheapest query, not the most expensive one, because the safe path should never be the slow path an owner learns to avoid.

findings.title: Default 'Privileged' Audit Log view forces a full sequential scan slower than the unfiltered noisy view
findings.evidence: Live EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) against the dev-stack public.audit_log (1,387,523 rows) for the exact _PRIVILEGED_CONSEQUENCE_SQL predicate in src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:86-97 shows `Parallel Seq Scan on audit_log ... Rows Removed by Filter: 460031 ... Execution Time: 695.137 ms` for the COUNT query alone. Repeated curl timing of GET /api/audit-log?limit=20&kind=privileged (the page's DEFAULT load, AuditLogPage.tsx:108 `...(showAllNoise ? {} : { kind: "privileged" })`) measured 0.49-0.92s consistently, versus 0.15-0.18s for the unfiltered call. `\d public.audit_log` confirms only single-column btree indexes exist (action, actor, ts DESC, target+ts) — none composite or partial that could support the OR-chain of `action LIKE '...%'` + `result = 'error'` conditions. The table is actively growing at high velocity (heartbeat rows land ~1ms apart per live sample), so this cost only worsens over time and the SAFE default view is punished, not the noisy opt-in one.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner opens /audit-log (loads with kind=privileged by default) and waits ~0.5-0.9s before any row renders, every single time, and the cost grows unbounded as audit_log accumulates rows — while switching to 'Showing all activity' (noise=all) is 3-6x faster despite returning far more data.

findings.title: Audit Log pagination is offset/limit with a full COUNT(*), diverging from the fleet's own keyset-pagination convention and degrading linearly with depth
findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/audit.py:351-513 `list_audit_log` takes `offset`/`limit`, runs `SELECT count(*) FROM public.audit_log{where_clause}` (line 481-488) then `... LIMIT ${idx} OFFSET ${idx+1}` (line 492-501) and returns `PaginationMeta(total=..., offset=..., limit=...)`. AuditLogPage.tsx:59,99-100,119-120 tracks `page` in component state and computes `totalPages = Math.ceil(total/PAGE_SIZE)`, with only Previous/Next buttons (lines 338-353) — no jump-to-page or jump-to-date control. Live EXPLAIN (ANALYZE) on an unfiltered `ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 20 OFFSET 500000` measured 669ms and scales with offset (`Index Scan ... rows=500020`). CLAUDE.md's own 'Cursor Pagination (BREAKING — Phase 2b, PR #1755)' convention already migrated /api/ingestion/events off exactly this pattern, and calendar_workspace.py / timeline.py already use `has_more`/`next_cursor` keyset shapes elsewhere in this codebase — Audit Log's endpoint never adopted it.
findings.failure_scenario: An owner searching audit history without knowing the right actor/action/date filter must click 'Next' repeatedly; each click both re-runs the full COUNT(*) and an increasingly expensive OFFSET-skip scan (measured 669ms at offset 500K on the unfiltered table, which the noise=all toggle exposes), with no faster route to older history than one page at a time.

findings.evidence: Backend: src/butlers/api/routers/sessions.py:279-314 (_attach_session_extras) computes `correction_count` from a real `corrections` table (alembic/versions/core/core_001_foundation.py:361-373: columns correction_type, target_session_id, correcting_session_id, description, status, summary, original_data_snapshot) and attaches it to every SessionDetail response. But frontend/src/api/types.ts's `SessionDetail` interface (line 240+) has NO `correction_count` field at all, and SessionDossier.tsx (the one dossier component shared by SessionDetailPage and the drawer) never references it. `grep -rln correction frontend/src/` shows the only frontend 'correction' surface is the unrelated chronicler episode-correction feature (CorrectionPromptsPanel, EpisodeDrawer) — a different table entirely. audits.page: /sessions + /sessions/:id (SessionsPage.tsx, SessionDetailPage.tsx, SessionDossier.tsx, SessionTable.tsx, SessionsPinnedStrip.tsx, SessionDetailDrawer.tsx)
audits.jarvis_gap: The surface is genuinely mature for what it does show: keyset pagination, URL-mirrored filters, bus-driven live refresh with a poll safety net, degraded-source honesty threaded through every fan-out (KPI, verdict, pinned strip, table), a shared one-dossier component with real root-evidence (process_log stderr/exit_code) instead of guessed tool-call names, and a working j/k/[/]/y keyboard loop. But it verifies only ONE axis of trust — 'did this session run and complete' — while silently omitting a second, more important axis the backend already computes: 'was this session's output later proven wrong.' A world-class JARVIS trace spine treats a correction as importantly as a failure: a session dossier should show, alongside StatusBadge, a 'Corrected' badge with type (data_correction/memory_deletion/misroute/action_reversal) and a link to the correcting session, so a green session is never trusted more than the system itself trusts it. It should also let the owner pivot straight to 'show me every gpt-5.6-luna session in the last hour' when a model-routing incident is suspected, without leaving the page — filtering by model/complexity is as fundamental as filtering by butler or status once routing tiers exist. And a running session that has clearly overrun its expected shape should offer the owner a way to act, not just watch a clock.

findings.evidence: src/butlers/api/routers/settings_console.py:308 emits `action_route="/secrets?tab=runtimes"` for every CLI-auth-needs-reauth item. The word 'runtimes' does not exist anywhere in pages.tsx's UI vocabulary either — CLI credentials are keyed `c:cli-auth/<provider>` in the spine (DirectionPassport.tsx:186-201 even has a legacy-canonicalization step from stale `s:` deep links to the current `c:` prefix, proving the real, current deep-link contract is `?focus=c:cli-auth/<id>`, not `?tab=`). Clicking 'Review →' on this item lands the owner on /secrets with no focus, no scroll, no highlight — they must manually hunt all ~34 credential rows (system:27, cli:3, user:4, per live GET /api/secrets/inventory) to find the one broken CLI runtime.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner sees the red 'CLI runtime needs re-authentication' banner (as they do right now, live), clicks Review, lands on a generic /secrets passport with no indication of which of 34 rows is broken — the exact five-second-verification promise the console exists to deliver is broken at its most urgent signal.

audits.page: Chat/conversation surface (frontend/src/components/chat/ — FloatingChatWidget.tsx, ChatPanel.tsx, MessageThread.tsx, ConversationHeader.tsx, ConversationList.tsx) + backend src/butlers/api/routers/conversations.py
audits.jarvis_gap: The widget is architecturally honest (no fabricated data, real error taxonomy) but is not actually a conversational front door: it only serves two narrow lanes (statement/correction, bug report) with no query/Q&A capability, invites free-form chat via generic copy while silently declining anything outside those lanes, shows the wrong butler identity while you're mid-conversation, fakes streaming over a poll loop, and lets 'Stop' cancel only the client's view of the work while the underlying spawned session (and any side effects) runs to completion unseen. An owner who tries to use it like Telegram — asking a question, expecting to see who's answering, expecting Stop to actually stop something — hits all four gaps in a single session.

findings.title: Widget invites free-form chat but silently declines anything outside the two lanes, live-confirmed
findings.evidence: Live conversation 019e2246-7f41-754e-a991-63fc7adf334b (GET /api/butlers/switchboard/conversations/.../messages): owner asked "what was i doing on saturday at 7pm" (a plain query the system's own chronicles/timeline data could answer) and got back: "I wasn't able to figure out how to handle that message — it's been filed for manual review (case ref: 3948e6dd). Try rephrasing, or say more explicitly what you'd like recorded or reported." Source: src/butlers/modules/pipeline.py:1240 `_dead_letter_dashboard_unroutable`, line ~1304 f-string "filed for manual review{case_note}...". MessageInput.tsx:29 placeholder is generic "Type a message..." and the widget title (FloatingChatWidget.tsx:383) is "Talk to Butlers" — nothing in the UI signals the two-lane (statement-correction / bug-report) scope constraint before the owner types.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner types any ordinary question ("what's my next appointment", "how much did I spend on X") expecting an assistant reply; gets a generic decline + case reference instead, every time, with no in-UI hint this was ever going to happen.

findings.title: Active-thread header shows the wrong butler identity — 'switchboard' hardcoded, real routed_butler only visible in history list
findings.evidence: ConversationHeader.tsx:48-70 renders `{butlerName}` where FloatingChatWidget.tsx:451-456 always passes `butlerName={WIDGET_BUTLER}` (WIDGET_BUTLER = "switchboard", line 90) regardless of which domain butler actually handled the message. `conversation.routed_butler` (the real answer) is only rendered in ConversationList.tsx:92-100 as a badge in the history view — never in the active thread you are chatting in. Live-confirmed via API: GET /api/butlers/switchboard/conversations returns `routed_butler: null` even on a 4-message thread that received an assistant reply, so even the one place that shows routing can be uninformatively null.
findings.failure_scenario: Owner corrects a relationship fact, it routes to the relationship butler, but the open thread's header still reads "switchboard" the entire time — multi-butler routing visibility, one of the explicit flagship asks for this surface, is invisible in the one view an owner is actually looking at.

findings.title: Stop button doesn't stop anything — it detaches the client's poll loop while the spawned session and its side effects run to completion
findings.evidence: Frontend: FloatingChatWidget.tsx handleStop() (line 343-345) only calls `abortRef.current?.abort()` on the fetch AbortController; the AbortError handler (lines 316-321) sets `interrupted: true` then clears streaming after 1500ms with no further server call. Backend: conversations.py `_stream_conversation_response` (lines 257-412) already submitted the envelope to Switchboard in Step 2 (line 291, before the poll loop even starts) and the poll loop's only reaction to client disconnect (line 361-363, `await request.is_disconnected()`) is to `return` — no cancellation call, no session/tool termination anywhere in this file or conversations.py (grepped for cancel/terminate/kill — zero hits). The routed butler's session (and any route_to_butler side effect, e.g. recording a correction) keeps running for up to `_SESSION_TIMEOUT_S = 300.0` (line 128) and its reply gets persisted and will simply appear in the thread on the next open/refetch with no acknowledgment it was ever "interrupted."
findings.failure_scenario: Owner sends a data correction, realizes it's wrong mid-send, clicks Stop, sees "Interrupted" and believes nothing happened — but the domain butler session is still executing the correction and will complete it regardless; the owner has no way to actually cancel a dispatched action from this surface.

findings.title: "Streaming" is cosmetic: the whole reply arrives as one SSE 'token' event, not incremental generation
findings.evidence: conversations.py:397-400: "Step 4: Emit the already-persisted conversation_reply — no DB write happens here" followed by a single `yield _sse_event("token", {"content": reply_row["content"]})` carrying the entire completed reply text in one shot. The frontend's token handler (FloatingChatWidget.tsx:282-289, MessageThread.tsx TypingIndicator/streaming state) is built around per-token appends (`content: prev.content + token`) and a typing indicator, visually implying live token-by-token generation, but with a 0.5s poll interval (_POLL_INTERVAL_S=0.5) and up to 300s session timeout, the actual experience is: typing indicator for anywhere from ~10s to 5 minutes, then the full answer appears at once. This is a materially different (and less honest about latency) UX than what the streaming-shaped code implies.
findings.failure_scenario: For long-running domain-butler sessions, the owner watches a typing indicator with zero incremental signal for up to 5 minutes before anything renders — worse perceived latency than Telegram, which at least shows delivery/read receipts, and the UI's own streaming affordance (TypingIndicator, token accumulator) misrepresents what's actually happening server-side.

audits.page: Ecosystem lens: eco:collaboration — cross-butler delegation, context bus, insight broker, briefing aggregation (Switchboard + MCP-only doctrine)
audits.jarvis_gap: A world-class JARVIS is more than the sum of its specialists: a question in one domain silently pulls what it needs from another, a life-event in one domain ripples to every domain it touches, and the fleet gets smarter each time two butlers figure something out together. Butlers has built the full scaffolding for this — a delegation ledger (ask/answer/route), a situational context bus, an insight broker, a briefing-aggregation view — but ZERO genuine cross-butler collaboration actually happens. The one true bidirectional primitive, the delegation ledger, has 0 rows in its entire lifetime (live-confirmed) because (a) no butler is ever told the tool exists and (b) even if used, the answer lands in a table the asking butler never reads and is never woken to consume. The context bus is one-directional awareness (signals in, prompt-preamble out); the briefing view is a passive union of siloed paragraphs that never cross-reference. Nothing composes. The gap is not missing plumbing — it is that the plumbing carries no water: no activation prompts, no return-of-answer loop, no compounding memory, no cross-domain ripple. The system is a set of soloists with a stage and a mic they never use.

findings.title: Delegation ledger has 0 rows in its entire lifetime — the fleet's only bidirectional collaboration primitive is inert (PROMOTION of run-05 finding, with new mechanism + live confirmation)
findings.evidence: Live: GET http://127.0.0.1:42200/api/delegation/ledger?limit=5 returns {"data":[],"meta":{"total":0}}. NEW mechanism 1 (root cause): grep across all of roster/ (CLAUDE.md, MANIFESTO.md, .agents/skills) for delegate_ask/delegate_receive/delegation returns ZERO hits — the tool is registered fleet-wide (src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:55-68, non-STAFFER gate) but no butler prompt or skill ever tells a butler the tool exists or when to reach for it. It is dead by construction. NEW mechanism 2: the return loop is architecturally absent — delegate_answer (_delegation.py:330-363) calls only record_answer() which UPDATEs the ledger row; there is no notify(), no scheduled wake-task for asking_butler. The asker's ephemeral session that called delegate_ask ended after receiving {"status":"routed"}; the answer lands in a table nobody reads.
findings.detail: This is the exact 'delegation onto the trace spine (0 rows ever)' run-05 queued first-in-line. Promotion warranted: run-05 had only 'still 0 rows'; I add (a) live re-confirmation, (b) the precise dual root cause (no prompt surface + no return loop), and (c) a proven-fix precedent: context_producers.py:1-9 documents that public.user_context sat at 0 rows for 3.5 months while three consumers read it, until a deterministic producer layer 'lit the bus.' The delegation ledger is the identical pathology, unfixed.

findings.title: The cross-butler-delegation spec has NO 'wake the asker' requirement — Discoverability ends at a dashboard list
findings.evidence: openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md: the Discoverability requirement's three scenarios are all read-side (GET /api/delegation/ledger list, GET one by id, 404 on unknown) — the asker is expected to 'check back later (dashboard delegation ledger, or ask the target directly)' per _delegation.py:100-102. There is no requirement, tool, or scheduled task that returns the answer to the butler that asked. The loop is open by specification, not just by omission.
findings.detail: Because butler sessions are ephemeral, 'check back later' means 'never' unless a future scheduled session of the asker happens to re-ask and manually poll the ledger by an id it no longer holds. The spec formalizes a write-only answer. Fixing this requires a spec amendment (add a 'Wake The Asker' requirement), not just code.

findings.title: Every collaboration primitive except delegation is one-directional; nothing composes across domains
findings.evidence: Context bus (openspec/specs/context-bus/spec.md, src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py): deterministic producers WRITE signals, spawner_context.py:296 READS them into a prompt preamble — awareness flows one way, no butler acts on another's transition. Insight broker (openspec/specs/insight-delivery): butlers propose candidates → broker dedups → digest via notify — one way to the user, never butler-to-butler. Briefing aggregation (openspec/specs/cross-butler-briefing-aggregation): general.v_briefing_contributions is a read-only UNION of each schema's OWN briefing/daily/% state — N siloed paragraphs, no section can reference another domain.
findings.detail: The Switchboard's mandate (vision.md:9-11: 'brokers proactive insights from domain butlers, and maintains shared situational awareness so butlers adapt') is only half-built: shared awareness exists as a read-only signal bus, but the 'brokering' is user-facing digest delivery, never a butler consuming another butler's output to do something it could not do alone.

moves.title: Close and activate the delegation loop: wake-the-asker return path + prompt surface + one deterministic seed
moves.why: Turns the fleet's only bidirectional primitive from a 0-row corpse into a live collaboration spine. The proven precedent is context_producers.py, which lit an identically-dead bus. Payoff: relationship butler drafting a gift can actually pull finance's budget; health can pull travel's trip dates — cross-domain reasoning that no single butler can do. Without this, every other collaboration idea is built on a tool nobody uses.
moves.integration_points: (1) Return path: extend delegate_answer in src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:330 so record_answer success schedules a one-shot wake-task for asking_butler (reuse scheduler.schedule_create exactly as delegate_receive:314 already does for the target) whose prompt hands the session the question+answer and instructs it to act; OR notify() the owner when the delegated answer resolves an owner-facing question. (2) Prompt surface: add a shared skill roster/*/.agents/skills/cross-butler-delegation/SKILL.md + a CLAUDE.md clause ('when a decision needs another domain's knowledge you don't own, delegate_ask instead of guessing'). (3) Spec: add a 'Wake The Asker' requirement to openspec/specs/cross-butler-delegation/spec.md. (4) One deterministic seed use-case (e.g. relationship gift-brainstorm skill calls delegate_ask finance for budget) to prove the round trip end-to-end.
moves.slice_plan: Slice A: return-path (delegate_answer → wake-task) + spec amendment + test that an answered row wakes the asker. Slice B: skill + CLAUDE.md prompt surface across domain butlers. Slice C: one seeded real use-case (gift budget) producing the first non-test ledger rows in production.

moves.title: Cross-referential briefing: let each specialist's briefing contribution pose one cross-domain delegate_ask whose answer enriches its section
moves.why: The morning briefing is today N siloed paragraphs (general.v_briefing_contributions is a bare UNION). Genuine collaboration makes it connected: health's section can note 'your pharmacy spend is up 40% this week' by asking finance; travel's section can note 'your Tokyo trip overlaps Kenji's birthday' by asking relationship+calendar. The owner reads one coherent life-picture instead of seven disconnected reports — the JARVIS 'it sees the whole board' effect.
moves.integration_points: src/butlers/jobs/briefing.py (the briefing assembly job, SPECIALIST_BUTLERS list) + the now-activated delegation ledger. Each specialist's briefing session may issue at most one delegate_ask; the briefing job joins answers back on the ledger before composing. Reuses the delegation trace spine — no parallel path — satisfying the MCP-only doctrine (architecture.md:51).
moves.slice_plan: Depends on the delegation loop being closed (prior move). Slice 1: allow one delegate_ask per specialist briefing, budget-gated. Slice 2: briefing composer joins ledger answers into the contributing section. Slice 3: cap/anti-spam so a briefing can't fan out unboundedly.

moves.title: Delegated Q&A feeds the shared memory catalog — collaboration that compounds
moves.why: Right now delegate_answer just closes a ledger row; the knowledge the answering butler produced evaporates. If each answered Q&A were written back into public.memory_catalog (the SAME hybrid index that resolves_target_via_catalog already reads at delegation_ledger.py:261-304), the fleet would LEARN from every collaboration: the next similar question routes faster and can be served from the cached answer instead of waking a butler. This is the compounding-intelligence property — the system gets smarter each time two butlers figure something out together — that distinguishes a JARVIS from a phone tree.
moves.integration_points: delegate_answer in src/butlers/core_tools/_delegation.py:330 → on success, write a low-confidence 'delegated_qa' catalog entry (owned by answering_butler, source_butler set) via butlers.core.memory_hooks (the same dependency-inverted writer the search side uses). Guard against pollution: mark provenance='delegated_qa', low confidence, TTL/decay so stale answers don't masquerade as current authority (honors the north-star 'staleness never wears current-data authority').
moves.slice_plan: Slice 1: write answered Q&A to catalog with explicit low-confidence provenance + test that it surfaces in Fleet Knowledge search tagged as delegated. Slice 2: resolve_target_via_catalog / delegate_ask short-circuits to a cached answer when a high-similarity delegated_qa entry exists, recording the cache-hit on the new ledger row for the trace spine.

moves.title: Standing cross-domain subscriptions on the context bus — the life-event ripple, re-grounded on existing single-writer signals
moves.why: Delegation is one-shot pull; genuine proactivity is push: a butler registers a STANDING interest in another domain's signal transitions so a life-event in one domain automatically ripples to every domain it touches (travel sets traveling→relationship surfaces contacts in that city; health sets sick→general reschedules commitments). Run-05 cut 'life-event ripple pub/sub' as too vague; this re-proposal is materially more concrete because it reuses the ALREADY-BUILT context bus (public.user_context, single-writer discipline, TTL, the deterministic producer job as the publish point) instead of inventing a new bus.

The context producer job in src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py, at each set_context transition, checks subscriptions and schedules a wake-task for the subscriber (same scheduler primitive delegate_receive uses). audits.ideal: Genuine collaboration means: (1) a butler that needs another domain's knowledge asks for it and RECEIVES the answer in-band — the delegation ledger's ask→route→answer→WAKE-THE-ASKER loop is closed and every domain butler is prompted to reach for it; (2) the answer the fleet computes together is remembered — delegated Q&A flows back into the shared memory catalog so collaboration compounds; (3) briefings and decisions are cross-referential, not siloed — a section can pull what it needs from a sibling domain over the same trace spine; (4) life-events ripple — a standing subscription on the context bus turns one domain's signal transition into proactive action in every domain it touches. All of this rides the two sanctioned coordination surfaces (Switchboard route() and the public-schema bus/ledger/catalog) — no parallel channel, honoring MCP-only doctrine. The measure: the delegation_ledger stops being empty, and the owner experiences one system that reasons across domains, not seven soloists.

audits.page: Ecosystem lens: eco:reliability (scheduler, deadman patterns, escalation flow, QA patrol, connector/producer liveness) — first dedicated sweep since run-03
audits.jarvis_gap: The fleet has built a genuinely broad deadman apparatus (calendar-sync, external, migration-drift, connector-offline, butler-heartbeat, backup, secrets, model checks) — far more than run-05's "adjacent evidence points down" implied. But it lacks the one doctrine that makes reliability *earned*: a level-triggered attention lifecycle. Live, a chronic infra failure is escalated exactly ONCE and then every subsequent 30-min tick observes the still-broken state and deliberately does nothing (`reason: already_escalated`) — so the calendar-sync outage the fleet built a bespoke deadman for (bu-hmdqz.10) is live and unescalated 9+ days on, finance/switchboard ~110 days on, its only signal a single week-old case buried in a QA table. Simultaneously the OTHER half of the apparatus does the opposite — re-investigating one known-dead connector 67 times with LLM sessions that all end `unfixable`. And the whole apparatus is a single unsupervised process (dashboard-api, fire-and-forget asyncio tasks, no restart-on-death) whose only external watcher-of-the-watchers (external_deadman) is switched off. The result violates the north star directly: failure impersonates health as it ages, and staleness wears current-data authority (the week grid still renders a 110-day-old snapshot).

findings.title: Escalate-once doctrine → chronic infra failures go permanently silent (calendar outage live & unescalated 9+ days; finance/switchboard 110+ days)
findings.evidence: Live dashboard-api log (19:21:18): calendar_sync_deadman_check → {'available': True, 'stale': True, 'escalated': False, 'reason': 'already_escalated', 'first_detected_at': '2026-07-13T13:44:30'}. DB: public.audit_log has calendar_sync_deadman_escalated (2 rows, last 2026-07-13 14:36) and 2 CalendarSyncDeadman healing_attempts (unfixable, 2026-07-13). Live provider freshness: finance/provider_event last_synced 2026-03-30..04-07 (~114d), switchboard 2026-03-30, health/messenger/travel 2026-07-14 (8d) — all ≫ the 10-min threshold (DEFAULT_SYNC_INTERVAL_MINUTES=5 × PROJECTION_STALENESS_MULTIPLIER=2, src/butlers/modules/calendar.py:106-110). Same pattern for migration_drift (chronicler/memory mem_009 missing, escalated once 2026-07-17, still drifted). The behavior is codified: openspec/specs/deployment-and-drift/spec.md:155-156 mandates 'subsequent ticks do not re-escalate it'. grep for re-escalat|aging|days_open|re_notify across src/butlers/core|jobs returns nothing.
findings.detail: maybe_escalate_calendar_sync_deadman (src/butlers/jobs/calendar_sync_deadman.py:294-299) returns already_escalated forever once a fingerprint has one escalated marker. There is no severity aging, no re-notification, no owner re-surface as the unresolved condition ages. A 9-day-old unfixable row is not earned calm — the system knows the calendar is dead and has chosen to stay quiet.

findings.title: Connector-offline re-investigation churn: 67 unfixable LLM investigations for ONE dead connector
findings.evidence: DB: public.healing_attempts WHERE exception_type='ConnectorOffline' GROUP BY call_site → connector:telegram_user_client/telegram:user:@Tzeusy = 67 rows (latest 2026-07-22 01:04), plus google_health sub-endpoints, owntracks. Totals: 66 unfixable + 7 pr_open + 3 timeout + 1 failed across ConnectorOffline. Cooldown default = 60 min (src/butlers/core/healing/dispatch.py:133,159); get_recent_attempt (src/butlers/core/healing/tracking.py:454-492) only suppresses within that window, and each terminal 'unfixable' closes the attempt so the next patrol re-discovers the SAME fingerprint as novel and dispatches another LLM QA investigation. InfraStateSource is a full DiscoverySource in the patrol→triage→dispatch pipeline (src/butlers/core/qa/sources/infra_state.py:16-21).
findings.detail: The inverse of finding #1: a known-unfixable ops condition (dead connector process) is re-classified as a novel code bug every 60 min, burning an LLM investigation each time (also note 7 ConnectorOffline attempts reached pr_open — a code PR cannot fix a dead connector process). No 'known-open infra condition, suppress re-investigation' memory exists. Same root doctrine gap, opposite symptom.

findings.title: The reliability apparatus is a single unsupervised process with its only external watcher switched off
findings.evidence: Every deadman/drift loop is a fire-and-forget asyncio task in the dashboard-api process with add_done_callback(_BACKGROUND_TASKS.discard) and NO restart-on-death (src/butlers/api/app.py:308-309,433-434,456-457,482 and 6 more; grep restart|supervis in app.py → none). external_deadman (the only check that crosses the egress path to prove the host can reach the outside world — src/butlers/jobs/external_deadman.py:1-44) is disabled: DB shows zero external_deadman_ping_success rows ever, and InfraStateSource._check_external_deadman returns [] silently when EXTERNAL_DEADMAN_URL is unset (infra_state.py:386-387).
findings.detail: If the dashboard-api process dies or a loop task escapes its try, every deadman (calendar, drift, connector, heartbeat, backup, secrets, model) dies with it and nothing external notices — the exact 'watcher must survive the failure it watches' argument the calendar deadman docstring makes, applied to the watcher itself. The one component built to close that gap is off by default and treated as a legitimate absence, not a standing recommendation.

findings.title: Whole-daemon heartbeat ≠ per-producer liveness: a live butler can host a dead sub-task invisibly
findings.evidence: Live: switchboard.butler_registry shows finance eligibility_state=active, last_seen 2026-07-22 19:34 (1 min ago) — yet finance's calendar provider sync is 114 days dead and finance has 3 enabled scheduled tasks with next_run_at up to 115 days in the past. The heartbeat deadman (InfraStateSource._check_butler_heartbeats, infra_state.py:238-306) recomputes staleness from butler_registry.last_seen_at only — it cannot see a single wedged poller/producer inside a heartbeating daemon. Only calendar has a bespoke per-producer deadman (calendar_sync_deadman.py), and it escalates once (finding #1).
findings.detail: Coverage hole: the sync poller, the shared context_producers (src/butlers/jobs/context_producers.py — 'shared situational awareness', vision.md:10), and the event-consumption path all live inside daemons that report healthy. There is no generic per-producer freshness deadman; each producer that dies silently is invisible until someone builds a one-off module (as calendar did) — and even then it only fires once.

findings.title: Connector registry stores a stale-but-'healthy' state column that contradicts derived liveness
findings.evidence: Live public.v_qa_connector_state: telegram_user_client/@Tzeusy state='healthy' with last_heartbeat_at 2026-07-18 03:39 (age 4d15h); google_health has 6 sub-connectors state='unknown' with NULL heartbeat and one 'error' at 9d18h. InfraStateSource correctly recomputes via derive_liveness rather than trusting the column (infra_state.py:207-208, docstring 39-44 makes the same argument for heartbeats), precisely because the stored column can 'sit stale forever'.
findings.detail: Any UI or reader that trusts the stored `state` column (rather than deriving liveness fresh) will render a 4-day-stale connector as healthy — failure impersonating health. Either eagerly reconcile the column or never display it; today it is a latent all-clear lie.

findings.title: Deadline-type scheduled tasks linger enabled long past target with no lifecycle cleanup
findings.evidence: Live: finance.scheduled_tasks — tenancy_deposit_to_landlord (next_run_at 2026-03-29, 115d overdue), IBKR SPCE filing/recovery (2026-05-11/05-16), all task_type='deadline', enabled=true, last_result NULL; relationship SUTD Homecoming 2026 registration 6d overdue. These pollute the enabled-count and any overdue-schedule signal (#3466 surfaces overdue facts in src/butlers/api/routers/butlers.py, display-only).
findings.detail: Distinct from scheduler wedging (all cron tasks have future next_run_at — the scheduler is firing). This is deadline-task lifecycle hygiene: a passed one-shot deadline should auto-disable/archive so it stops masquerading as an overdue recurring producer.

moves.title: Establish a Reliability Doctrine spec with a level-triggered escalation-aging ladder (replace escalate-once)
moves.why: Directly closes the critical gap: an unresolved infra condition must be re-surfaced with rising urgency the longer it stays broken, and auto-resolved with an owner-visible 'recovered after N days' when it clears — instead of one silent case. Serves vision.md north star ('failure never impersonates health, staleness never wears current-data authority') and What-Success-Looks-Like ('recover from transient failures'). Amends the doctrine that currently mandates the failure.
moves.slice_plan: 1) New openspec capability change 'reliability-doctrine' (or amend deployment-and-drift) defining the condition lifecycle open→aging(L1..Ln)→resolved and the re-escalation ladder (e.g. re-notify at 1d/3d/7d, severity bump). 2) Shared escalation_aging helper computing age from first_detected + last escalated marker in public.audit_log. 3) Rewire calendar_sync_deadman.maybe_escalate_* and deploy_drift to consult it instead of returning already_escalated forever. 4) Aging re-notifications route through the owner-attention quiet-window predicate from the in-flight consolidate-owner-attention-policy change so they respect quiet hours.

moves.why: One table fixes BOTH the silent-forever gap (finding #1) and the 67x re-investigation churn (finding #2): a condition that is 'open' suppresses redundant LLM re-investigation while the aging ladder handles owner re-surfacing, and 'recovered' auto-closes it. Turns two contradictory ad-hoc mechanisms (direct-to-healing_attempts escalate-once vs patrol-re-discover-every-hour) into one coherent lifecycle. Serves the QA staffer infrastructure contract (failure modes + escalation procedures per vision.md:26-29).

A watcher that can't survive the failure it watches isn't a watcher. Serves vision non-negotiable #4 (the daemon is reliable, testable, predictable infrastructure).

moves.why: Closes finding #4 uniformly: today a live daemon can host a dead sub-task (sync poller, context producer, event consumer) invisibly, and the only cure is hand-building a bespoke module per producer. audits.ideal: World-class reliability for a one-person JARVIS is a single level-triggered attention lifecycle for every infra condition. A producer/schedule/connector/migration is either provably fresh, or it is an OPEN condition with an age. Open conditions are: notified once, never wastefully re-investigated by an LLM, re-surfaced to the owner with rising urgency the longer they stay unresolved, and auto-closed with a visible 'recovered after N days' when they clear. Every background producer stamps a heartbeat against a declared cadence, so a live daemon can never hide a dead sub-task. The whole apparatus is supervised (loops restart on death) and has at least one watcher that lives OUTSIDE the process it watches and crosses the egress path, so 'everything looks healthy but nothing is leaving the host' is detectable by construction. The five-second verdict for the owner is then honest at every age: a fresh outage escalates loudly, a 9-day outage escalates louder — never quieter — and a recovered one says so. Today the plumbing for most of this exists; the doctrine that makes it earned calm rather than fabricated calm does not.

audits.page: Ecosystem lens: knowledge-graph (memory module — promotion, decay, provenance, cross-butler reads)
audits.jarvis_gap: The memory subsystem stores a large corpus (4,689 facts, 7,450 episodes, 112 rules, 4,159 live catalog rows across 10 butlers) but it does not grow as a *trustworthy graph*. The north-star trace spine (signal -> session -> evidence) is absent or broken for the overwhelming majority of knowledge: 89-99% of facts carry no provenance edge at all, and of the citations that do exist, ~40-75% dangle to episodes that TTL-cleanup already deleted — so "why do you believe this?" returns nothing for a fact chosen at random, and returns a dead pointer for half of the rest. The graph is a star of entity->literal property facts (only 1.4-7% of facts are entity->entity edges), so traversal has almost nothing to traverse. Procedural memory is write-only: 112 rules are 100% `candidate`, 0 have ever promoted to established/proven or demoted to anti_pattern, applied_count/success_count/harmful_count are 0 across the whole fleet, and the mark_helpful/harmful feedback tools have no runtime caller — the maturity lifecycle the docs advertise is decoration. Breaking the consolidation ouroboros (#3454/#3455) reduced episode volume but changed none of this: the provenance and rule-quality failures are structural (no FK, no per-fact attribution, direct-store facts get no links), independent of the ouroboros. And none of it is measured: /api/memory/stats reports counts and catalog live/stale but has zero provenance-coverage, edge-density, dangling-citation, or rule-promotion-health signal, so failure wears the mask of a healthy-looking growing store.

findings.title: Provenance coverage collapse: 89-99% of facts have no traceable source
findings.evidence: Live SQL per schema (fact, facts_with_any_derived_from_prov, source_episode_id set): relationship 1798/6/7; general 378/15/75; finance 809/9/31; health 295/1/1; lifestyle 572/2/117. request_id present on only 100/1798 (rel), 10/295 (health), 203/809 (finance). Direct memory_store_fact writes create no memory_links row (only execute_consolidation calls create_link, consolidation_executor.py:154). Most facts cannot be traced to an originating session, episode, or evidence — the spine is absent, not just weak.
findings.detail: The 'unbroken trace spine (signal -> session -> evidence)' is the vision's load-bearing promise for earned calm; a fact you cannot trace is indistinguishable from a fabricated one.

findings.title: ~40-75% of the provenance edges that DO exist dangle to deleted episodes
findings.evidence: Live SQL (derived_from->episode links / dangling to missing episode): relationship 84/42 (50%), general 1384/528 (38%), lifestyle 138/103 (75%), finance 150/72 (48%). Root cause: run_episode_cleanup deletes episodes with a bare DELETE (consolidation.py:504,515-523); memory_links is polymorphic with NO foreign key (migrations/001_memory_schema.py:341-358), so nothing prunes or preserves the edge. Following a fact's citation after TTL yields an episode that no longer exists.
findings.detail: Provenance impersonates traceability: the edge is present so the fact looks cited, but the citation is dead. Staleness wears current-data authority.

findings.title: Batch-blur attribution: each fact is linked to ALL episodes in the batch, not its evidence
findings.evidence: consolidation_executor.py:154-155 and :199-200: `for episode_id in source_episode_ids: create_link(pool,'fact',new_fact_id,'episode',episode_id,'derived_from')` — source_episode_ids is the entire (tenant,butler) batch (up to DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE=100, consolidation.py:71). The parser's NewFact/UpdatedFact dataclasses (consolidation_parser.py:26-46) have no per-fact supporting-episode field, so evidence-level attribution is structurally impossible even if the LLM knew it.
findings.detail: A fact derived from one episode is cited to 100. This is the 500-episode batch-blur baseline queued by run-05, now source-confirmed at the exact call site.

findings.title: Procedural memory is write-only: 0 of 112 rules have ever promoted or been scored
findings.evidence: Live /api/memory/stats: total_rules 112, candidate_rules 112, established_rules 0, proven_rules 0, anti_pattern_rules 0. Live SQL: travel 70 rules + switchboard 36 rules, all candidate, sum(applied_count)=0, success=0, harmful=0. Zero '%rule%'/'%helpful%'/'%harmful%' rows in any schema's memory_events. grep: memory_mark_helpful/memory_mark_harmful referenced only in the module's own tool-registration files, no roster skill or runtime caller. rule_applications table dropped as write-orphaned (migrations/006).
findings.detail: docs/modules/memory.md advertises 'rules track maturity, effectiveness scores, application counts; harmful evidence weighted more heavily' but no spec requires a promotion loop and none runs live. memory_context feeds unproven candidate guidance as if it were learned knowledge. Promotes run-05's rule-application-loop spec-drift finding with fleet-wide live confirmation of a 100% dead loop.

findings.title: The graph is a star of property-facts, not a connected entity graph
findings.evidence: Live SQL (facts / entity_id set / object_entity_id set): relationship 1798/1760/57 (3.2% edges), general 378/375/27 (7%), finance 809/792/11 (1.4%), health 295/292/4 (1.4%). Only 1.4-7% of facts form an entity->entity edge; the rest are entity->literal properties.
findings.detail: memory_entity_neighbors and any concentration/graph-traversal read have almost nothing to traverse. KG 'growth' is fact-star accretion, not graph densification — confirms/quantifies run-05's object_entity_id-starvation note fleet-wide.

findings.title: No graph-quality metric is measured or surfaced anywhere
findings.evidence: Live /api/memory/stats returns only counts (episodes/facts/rules by state) + meta.catalog_live/stale/drifted. No provenance-coverage %, no dangling-citation count, no entity-edge density, no orphan-fact count, no rule-promotion health. The ann_observability job (memory.md:163) measures HNSW recall/churn but nothing about graph trustworthiness.
findings.detail: The owner cannot verify KG health in five seconds; a graph that is 95% untraceable and 50%-dangling renders as a healthy growing count. Failure looks like calm.

findings.title: memory-honesty-last-mile and open specs do NOT cover any of the above
findings.evidence: openspec/changes/memory-honesty-last-mile/proposal.md scopes 404/503 pool-failure semantics, exact paging totals, and dead-letter requeue — not provenance coverage, evidence durability, rule promotion, or edge density. module-memory/spec.md:82-83 mandates 'store rule as candidate with counts=0' but has no promotion requirement; :160-184 requires derived_from links but no per-fact attribution or TTL-durable evidence.
findings.detail: Confirms the proposals below are net-new, not duplicates of in-flight work.

moves.title: Per-fact evidence attribution + TTL-durable evidence digest
moves.why: Turns every consolidation-derived fact into a citation that names its actual supporting episode(s) AND survives episode cleanup, so 'why do you believe this?' has a real, non-rotting answer. Directly serves the vision trace-spine and the module-memory manifesto. Promotes run-05's queued KG candidate with the new live math (95% uncovered, ~50% dangling).
moves.integration_points: consolidation_parser.py (add supporting_episode_ids to NewFact/UpdatedFact/NewRule); prompt_template.py::build_consolidation_prompt (instruct the LLM to cite per-fact episode ids); consolidation_executor.py (link only cited episodes, not the whole batch); storage.store_fact + new facts.evidence JSONB column OR a memory_evidence table snapshotting {episode_id, observed_at, content_excerpt} at store time; new memory migration; module-memory/spec.md new Requirement 'Per-artifact provenance & durable evidence'.
moves.slice_plan: S1: schema field + parser + prompt (attribution only, links narrowed to cited episodes). S2: durable evidence snapshot column + write at store. S3: read surface (memory_get / inspect exposes evidence) + spec + tests. S4: backfill digest for existing facts from still-live episodes before they TTL.

moves.why: Makes '50% of citations are dead' structurally impossible: an episode can't be deleted while a fact still cites it without first converting the edge into a durable digest (dovetails with Move 1). Adds a store-side gate so a consolidation-derived fact with zero provenance is a logged failure, not a silent orphan — the calm-empty/never-drop-isError doctrine applied to the KG.

moves.title: Graph-quality observability: a memory_graph_health job + stats fields + console panel
moves.why: Extends five-second fleet verification to the KG. Owner sees provenance coverage %, dangling-citation count, entity-edge density, orphan-fact count, and rule-promotion distribution instead of a count that hides a 95%-untraceable graph. Serves earned-calm / single-pane.
moves.integration_points: New deterministic module-default job alongside ann_observability.py (read-only, per-schema); extend /api/memory/stats (src/butlers/api/routers memory) with provenance_coverage, dangling_provenance, edge_density, orphan_facts, rule_promotion_health under data/meta; frontend memory console panel; module-memory spec addition.
moves.slice_plan: S1: SQL metrics as a read-only job writing last_result. S2: surface in /api/memory/stats. S3: console panel + degraded-source honesty. S4: thresholds/warnings (coverage below X, dangling above Y).

moves.title: Decide the rule maturation loop: wire it or retire it
moves.why: 112 rules are 100% candidate forever and are still injected into memory_context as if learned — either close the loop so candidate->established->proven actually happens, or delete the maturity/effectiveness/count columns as zero-cruft decoration. Silent decoration is the one option the doctrine forbids. Needs an owner decision, not a silent default.

findings.title: No skip-link / bypass-blocks: keyboard users tab the entire sidebar on every navigation
findings.evidence: components/layout/Shell.tsx:89 renders `<main className="flex-1 overflow-y-auto p-6">` with no id and no tabindex; grep for `skip`/skip-link across components/layout/ and layouts/ returns only sr-only SheetTitle/DialogTitle — there is no 'skip to main content' affordance anywhere.
