findings.detail: WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass Blocks. Directly contradicts the keyboard-first north star. The shell already has the scaffolding for the fix (a single RootLayout mount point, a <main> element) — it just lacks a zero-cost skip link + a focus target. Generalizable: one link in RootLayout/Shell fixes it for every one of the ~40 pages.

findings.title: Focus-visibility floor is a no-op: `* { outline-ring/50 }` sets outline COLOR but never outline-STYLE, so raw buttons/links show no focus ring
findings.evidence: index.css:615 `@apply border-border outline-ring/50` sets `outline-color: var(--ring)/50%` only — outline-style stays `none`, so it renders nothing on :focus-visible. There is no base-layer `:focus-visible { outline }` rule (grep of index.css shows the sole `focus`/`outline` hit is line 615). Freshly-landed raw buttons therefore have invisible keyboard focus: SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:1144-1182 (webhook Edit/Disable/Test/Delete), :1030 (Add webhook), :447 (Full audit log link).
findings.detail: Promotes the known-standing focus-visible-floor finding with a NEW mechanism: the rule that LOOKS like a global focus floor is inert. The shared Button/Pill atoms carry their own focus-visible so they pass; every hand-rolled <button>/<a> across the app (see next finding) falls through to nothing. A single zero-specificity base rule `:where(a,button,[role=button],[tabindex]):focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ring);outline-offset:2px}` closes the floor app-wide and is override-safe.

findings.title: The 'text action-link' idiom (mono-uppercase hover:text-foreground button) is duplicated across 6+ surfaces with no shared atom and no focus ring
findings.evidence: Identical className pattern `font-mono text-[10-11px] uppercase tracking-wid* text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground transition-colors` on raw <button>/<summary> with NO focus-visible in: SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:1032,1148,1157,1170; SettingsConsolePage.tsx:166,178,358,406,465,605; health/MealTracker.tsx:423,434,490,498; health/MedicationTracker.tsx:448; settings/QaStafferCard.tsx:223,357; butler-detail/ButlerConfigTab.tsx:322. None import a shared component; each re-declares the styling by hand.
findings.detail: Built-once-never-generalized: the app's primary inline-action affordance has no component home, so the focus gap (previous finding) is reproduced by copy-paste on every new surface. An `<InlineActionLink>` atom (or the base-layer floor) would fix all instances and prevent regression. This is the cross-surface pattern the single-auditor lens is meant to catch.

findings.title: Data-table header association (scope) was built once and never generalized; shared TableHead primitive omits it
findings.evidence: Of 11 files containing `<th>` only components/approvals/attention-ledger-panel.tsx uses `scope=`. The shared primitive components/ui/table.tsx:53 `TableHead` renders a bare `<th>` with no default `scope="col"`. Freshly-landed permissions matrix SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:336-346 emits column `<th>` with no scope, and the row header (permission name) at :352 is a `<td>`, not `<th scope="row">` — a 2D grid with neither axis associated. Webhooks table :1055-1071 same (no scope).
findings.detail: Screen-reader table navigation cannot announce which butler/permission a cell belongs to from structure (the permission-matrix cells are salvaged only because each cell button carries a hand-written aria-label; the webhooks/spend/entity tables have no such backstop). Mechanism: default `scope="col"` in the TableHead primitive, add a `scope="row"` path, and migrate the raw <table> surfaces (SettingsPermissionsPage, SpendPage, EntitiesIndexPage, EntityDetailPage) onto it.

findings.title: Inherited permission-matrix cells render the state glyph at opacity-40, below the 3:1 non-text-contrast floor for a control's state indicator
findings.evidence: SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:369-370 applies `opacity-40` to inherited cells whose glyph is `text-muted-foreground` (index.css:45 `--muted-foreground: var(--mfg)`, a mid-gray). 40% opacity over the muted gray drops the ●/○ well under WCAG 1.4.11 3:1 in resting state; full opacity only on :hover.
findings.detail: Mitigated because grant state is dual-encoded (● vs ○ shape + per-cell aria-label), so this is a state-indicator-contrast nuance, not a color-only-signal failure. Fix: raise the inherited resting opacity floor (e.g. opacity-60) or convey 'inherited' with a border/weight token rather than transparency, so the dim treatment never crosses the contrast floor.

audits.page: Frontend-wide (accessibility lens): freshly-landed surfaces (health measurement doors #3486/#3481, approvals decision outcomes #3470, timeline maintenance lens #3462, permissions matrix #3473) + cross-surface patterns
audits.jarvis_gap: The freshly-landed surfaces individually landed accessible — approvals decision-outcome uses dl/dt/dd + aria-labelledby + real h3 (ApprovalsPage.tsx:721-771); the measurement trend is a keyboard tablist with per-arrow aria-labels, not an opaque SVG (MeasurementChart.tsx:297-400); OperationsNowList keeps role=list/listitem intact and uses role=alert only on the inner content for failures (OperationsNowList.tsx:70-179); the permission matrix is a semantic <table> whose cell buttons carry full aria-labels (SettingsPermissionsPage.tsx:365-378); reduced-motion has a real global floor (index.css:781) and the shell has a <main> landmark + a single aria-live announcer (Shell.tsx:89, RootLayout.tsx:44). The gap is NOT per-surface craft — it is that the accessibility primitives that would make calm keyboard verification universal were each built once and never generalized: focus visibility is an inert no-op rule so every hand-rolled control has an invisible ring, there is no skip link so the keyboard-first promise breaks on the sidebar, the text-action-link idiom has no component home so the focus gap re-appears on each new surface, and table header association exists in exactly one file. A world-class JARVIS makes accessibility a floor enforced by shared mechanisms (base-layer focus rule, shell skip link, one action-link atom, scope-defaulting table primitive), not a per-PR courtesy that the newest surface happens to remember.
audits.ideal: Accessibility is enforced by four shared mechanisms rather than re-earned per surface: (1) a zero-specificity base-layer :focus-visible outline floor so every interactive element — current and future, hand-rolled or atomic — shows a ring the moment it is keyboard-focused; (2) a shell skip link + focusable <main> so keyboard verification never pays the sidebar tax; (3) a single <InlineActionLink> atom that owns the mono-uppercase action affordance's focus ring, hit-target, and disabled state, killing the copy-paste idiom and a grep/eslint guard preventing its return; (4) a TableHead primitive that defaults scope='col' and supports scope='row', with all raw <table> surfaces migrated onto it. With these in place, a new surface is accessible by construction, and the five-second fleet verification is fully operable — and observable — by keyboard and screen reader alike.

audits.page: Frontend-wide (visual-language lens): Dispatch spec adherence across all of frontend/src
audits.jarvis_gap: The north star is "one visual language (Dispatch) built by one hand." Today the frontend runs two-and-a-half dialects that never merged: (1) Dispatch rule-separated surfaces on the converted pages; (2) an "informational blue/purple" dialect that Dispatch deliberately has no token for, thriving because the color-guard lint enumerates only the six WARM status shades and leaves the entire blue/purple/sky/violet/cyan/teal/rose half of Tailwind unguarded; (3) a forked state palette in the ingestion/connectors subtree that ships divergent fallback literals and hand-rolls the StateDot primitive; plus 49 files still on shadcn Card boxes instead of surfaces. The recent 07-17+ landings (DeploymentTile #3451 as a Card; TimelineLedger kind-dots as raw bg-blue-500/bg-purple-500) extended the forks rather than the language. Surfaces do not yet read as one hand because enforcement only covers the warm-status half of the problem.
audits.ideal: One enforced palette with zero un-tokened hues. The color-guard lint denies EVERY Tailwind named-palette utility (not just red/green/emerald/amber/yellow/orange), so a stray bg-blue-500 fails CI exactly as bg-red-500 does. There is no "informational blue": kind taxonomies resolve to --categorical-*, interactive CTAs resolve to --fg-inversion (the one commit button form), status resolves to StateDot/Sev + --red/--amber/--green. Status is rendered by exactly one primitive (StateDot/Sev) everywhere — the connector subtree, GoogleHealthStatusCard, topology, and timeline all import it rather than hand-rolling rounded-full spans with divergent oklch fallbacks. State color never appears in a bg- position outside the .attention-row tint+rail. Surfaces are rule-separated Dispatch sections/tiles with no rounded bordered Card boxes; a conformance lint blocks new ui/card imports on pages. Every var(--token) is bare — no var(--token, oklch(...)) fallback literals, because the tokens are always defined and the fallbacks only ever produce a second, off-brand palette.

findings.title: Color-guard lint enumerates only warm status shades; the entire cool half of Tailwind is unguarded, and an un-tokened 'informational blue/purple' dialect proliferates across 6+ surfaces
findings.evidence: frontend/eslint.config.js:58-78 STATUS_COLOR_SELECTORS regex alternates only (red|green|emerald|amber|yellow|orange); blue/purple/sky/violet/indigo/cyan/teal/rose/pink are absent, so these all pass CI: components/approvals/rule-promotion-banner.tsx:32,67 (bg-blue-50/30 dark:bg-blue-950/20 card + bg-blue-600 hover:bg-blue-700 text-white CTA), components/approvals/autonomy-suggestions-banner.tsx:65,102 (same), components/approvals/approval-teaching-digest.tsx:37 (bg-blue-500/5 panel, wired live via ApprovalsPage.tsx:74), components/ingestion/StatusBadge.tsx:74 (replay_pending bg-blue-500 text-white — while sibling error/failed use variant=destructive token), components/schedules/ScheduleTable.tsx:152 (bg-blue-600 'job' badge), components/butler-detail/ButlerQaInvestigationsTab.tsx:63 (bg-sky-400 text-white), components/timeline/TimelineLedger.tsx:63-65 (session bg-blue-500, notification bg-purple-500), components/ingestion/timeline/HourFlameStrip.tsx:213 (bg-blue-500). Dispatch has no blue token and no 'informational' semantic; the CTAs also violate Button Forms (commit = --fg bg, 'no rounded gradient CTA anywhere') and the cards violate Surfaces-not-cards.
findings.detail: The guard comment (eslint.config.js:41-57) states it fixed '80+ files using 2-3 different named greens for healthy' — it closed the warm/status side and left the cool/informational side entirely open, so blue became a de-facto fourth semantic (primary/new/info). The fix is a mechanism, not a site list: switch the selector from a 6-hue allow-enumeration to a full Tailwind-named-palette denylist with the existing line-level eslint-disable escape for genuine fixed categoricals.

findings.title: Category-hue confinement broken in TopologyGraph (butler-identity hue used as a STATUS color) and kind-taxonomy mis-tokened in TimelineLedger (raw Tailwind instead of --categorical-*)

Neither trips the current lint (category tokens aren't guarded outside a spec scenario; blue/purple aren't in the warm-shade selector).

Un-tokened hues become impossible, not just discouraged.

findings.title: Palette↔shortcut pairing has drifted: 5 pages have keyboard triage verbs, only 1 surfaces them in the command palette
findings.evidence: useListTriage (the shared j/k+verb hook) is adopted on 5 pages — DashboardPage.tsx:350-382 (a/d/x/u approve/deny/defer/undo), NotificationsPage.tsx:295-311 (a=Mark read), IssuesPage.tsx:228-247 (a=Acknowledge/Restore), DecisionsPage.tsx:193, ApprovalsPage.tsx (approve/deny/defer). Only ApprovalsPage.tsx:1703-1715 surfaces its verb in the palette WITH the binding shown (binding:["a"]). Notifications, Decisions, and Dashboard register NO palette commands at all (grep: no useRegisterCommands) — their keyboard verbs are invisible to ⌘K. Only 3 of 17 useRegisterCommands callers carry any binding: at all (ApprovalsPage:1711, CalendarWorkspacePage:4647/4656, ChroniclesPage:203/212/221).
findings.detail: The command-palette contract (discoverability subskill) is 'everything in menus is in the palette; displays each entry's keybinding inline — the palette is where shortcuts are learned.' The keys ARE shown in a per-page footer strip (ListTriageFooterHint) and the '?' sheet, but the palette — the cross-surface learning locus a keyboard-first operator lives in — mirrors neither. A user who opens ⌘K on the Dashboard (primary landing page) sees only global nav + RootLayout 'Trigger <butler>' actions, never approve/deny/defer/undo over the needs-attention list. Two discovery surfaces that disagree.

findings.title: IssuesPage palette command and keyboard verb are two divergent implementations of 'acknowledge' — different target, no binding shown
findings.evidence: IssuesPage.tsx:228-247 binds key 'a' = acknowledge/restore the SELECTED row (handler operates on `issues.find(i=>i.issue_key===selectedIssueKey)`). Separately, IssuesPage.tsx:318-331 registers palette command 'Acknowledge issue' that acts on `issues[0]` (the NEWEST issue), carries NO binding (so ⌘K never shows 'a'), and offers no restore variant when showDismissed. Same conceptual verb, two hand-written implementations with different targets, kept in sync by nobody.
findings.detail: This is the concrete failure mode of manual pairing: the palette entry and the keyboard entry drift into acting on different rows. Pressing 'a' acks the row you selected; running the identically-named palette command acks a different (newest) row. A keyboard-first user cannot trust the two surfaces to mean the same thing.

findings.title: The keyboard-shortcut chassis is the one 'built once' pattern with zero lint enforcement, while 7 sibling patterns each have a no-restricted-syntax guard
findings.evidence: eslint.config.js defines 8 selector groups enforced via no-restricted-syntax: HSL_VAR (23), STATUS_COLOR (58), HEX_COLOR (96), PRIMITIVE_REDECLARATION (126), HANDROLLED_OVERLAY (160), ANIMATE_PULSE (192), POLL_POLICY (234), FORMAT_CLONE (268). None ban raw addEventListener('keydown') (grep for keydown/addEventListener in eslint.config.js: 0 selector hits). The two registry docstrings explicitly state pairing is manual: command-registry.tsx:49-54 'setting this does NOT install any key handling'; use-register-shortcut.tsx:22-27 'nothing here auto-generates palette entries'.
findings.detail: Raw keydown has currently been fully eliminated (grep: only the 2 registries + shell hook use addEventListener keydown) — but by discipline, not enforcement. There is no guard against a new page hand-rolling keydown again, and no guard that a triage verb reaches the palette with its binding. Every other cross-surface invariant (colors, overlays, polling) is lint-enforced; the discoverability chassis, the newest and most-cited one (bu-qvnce.11, bu-86c4c.7), is not. Unenforced conventions decay — the Issues divergence above is the first crack.

moves.title: Make useListTriage the single source of truth for a verb: emit the paired palette command from the same declaration that installs the key
moves.why: Today a triage verb must be declared up to 4 times to be fully discoverable (key handler in ListTriageVerb, '?' entry, footer hint, palette command with binding) — and in practice only 1 of 5 pages does all 4, with Issues diverging outright. useListTriage already owns the verb list and already returns `hints` as the canonical set; extend ListTriageVerb with an optional `command?: { label; keywords? }`, and when present have the hook internally call useRegisterCommands with `binding` auto-derived from the verb's `key` and `perform` = the verb's own `handler`. One declaration → key handling + '?' sheet + footer hint + palette entry, all structurally guaranteed to share target, key, and label. This dissolves the Issues divergence (finding 2) by construction and backfills Notifications/Decisions/Dashboard palette entries (finding 1) for free.

Slice 2: adopt on IssuesPage — delete the separate useRegisterCommands block, add `command` to the verb; assert palette 'Acknowledge' now targets the selected row and shows 'a'. audits.jarvis_gap: The command palette is meant to be the one place where every action and its shortcut are learned ('the palette is where shortcuts are learned' — discoverability subskill). The cheapest wins (flip the Spotify podcast drop; add a youtube scope_set to the existing google registry) are small, and the highest-leverage new one (GitHub occupation) is a well-paved M following the steam_accounts pattern.

findings.title: Route-level code splitting built for only 3 of 39 pages — first paint ships the entire app
findings.evidence: router-config.tsx eagerly `import`s 39 page modules (lines 16-54); only CalendarWorkspacePage, ChroniclesPage, SystemPage use `lazy()` (router-config.tsx:68-70). The stale dist confirms the blast radius: dist/assets/index-*.js is 2,572,493 bytes uncompressed / 696,937 gzip — one monolith holding Health, Memory, Ingestion, QA, Entities, Education, Spend etc. Because eager pages statically import recharts (SessionsPage→SessionStripeChart) and xyflow (via router-config), the vendor-charts/vendor-graph splits added in vite.config.ts:37-38 still land in the initial dependency graph. The lazy discipline already exists one level down (all ButlerDetail tabs, MapWidget, GanttSwimlane are lazy) — it was simply never applied at the page router level.
findings.detail: Backend is fast (butlers/board 96ms warm, most endpoints <250ms live-confirmed), so the worst real wait a returning operator sees is parsing/executing a ~2.5MB JS bundle on cold load, not the API. Visiting Overview downloads code for pages the operator may never open this session.

findings.title: No background-poll suppression — ~71 literal-interval + 34 bus-aware queries keep firing on hidden tabs; only 2 hooks opt out
findings.evidence: grep of hooks/ (non-test): 71 query configs use a numeric-literal `refetchInterval` (use-finance 60s×5, use-memory 30s/15s, use-education 30s×many, use-system 60s/120s, use-qa STALE_TIME, use-owntracks 60s, use-butler-logs 5s...) and 34 use bus-aware/token intervals — but only use-education.ts and use-google-health.ts set `refetchIntervalInBackground: false`. lib/query-client.ts sets no such default (staleTime 30_000, retry 1 only). TanStack's default keeps every interval running when document.hidden, so a backgrounded dashboard tab hammers the API with ~100 recurring fetches indefinitely.
findings.detail: 'Background' means the tab is not visible — nobody is reading. A wall-mounted always-on display stays visible and is unaffected. No polling surface was identified that must stay live while hidden, so a single QueryClient default flips the whole app to honest 'poll only when watched' in one line, with per-query opt-in as the escape hatch (the inverse of today's per-hook opt-out that reached 2 of ~105 sites).

findings.title: Suspense fallbacks are three ad-hoc text divs, not one skeleton — perceived-nav is inconsistent and blocks generalizing lazy-loading
findings.evidence: router-config.tsx:94/157/206 each hand-write a different fallback string ('Loading calendar…', 'Loading chronicles…', 'Loading system…') as a bare `<div role="status" className="p-6 text-sm text-muted-foreground">`. There is no shared RouteSuspense/skeleton primitive. Eager pages appear instantly; these three flash raw text — an inconsistent nav feel, and the missing shared fallback is exactly what makes lazifying the other 36 pages feel like a regression rather than a win.

findings.title: Prefetch-on-intent plumbing generalizes but its target map covers only 4 routes; the highest-traffic drill-ins are no-ops
findings.evidence: usePrefetchOnIntent is attached unconditionally in RowLink.tsx, DisclosureRow.tsx, SessionTable.tsx, EntityFinder.tsx (good — the hook design is generalized). But lib/prefetch-registry.ts's MATCHERS resolve targets for only /sessions/:id, /approvals/:id, /timeline, and /ingestion?event= . Every RowLink to /butlers/:name, /entities/:id, /memory/facts/:factId, /memory/episodes/:episodeId, /memory/rules/:ruleId (router-config.tsx:81,122-124) resolves to null (no-op). The scaffolding is done; the data map that makes hover-to-warm actually fire on the busiest drill targets is 4 entries deep.
findings.detail: Distinct from the known-standing 'intent-prefetch wired 3 components deep' (which is about how many components attach the hook): here the components attach it correctly but the registry starves them of targets. Each detail page already has a single well-known fetch (useButlerDetail, useEntity, useFact) whose queryKey/queryFn could be reused verbatim, same pattern the 4 existing matchers use.

audits.ideal: A returning operator's console is interactive within a second on cold load because each page's JS arrives only when routed to (or hover-prefetched), and stays quiet — never polling while unwatched — while a single multiplexed socket keeps every visible, bus-covered surface live to the beat. The fast paths that already exist (one shared event-cache-registry invalidation spine, optimistic-mutation primitives, keepPreviousData pagination, intent-prefetch, bus-aware polling) are applied uniformly to every surface, not a measured subset, so no page is a second-class citizen on speed.
audits.jarvis_gap: Five-second fleet verification assumes the pane paints fast and updates without waste. The live spine here is genuinely world-class — one RootLayout socket, a declarative event→cache-patch registry, tested optimistic primitives, intent-prefetch scaffolding. But every one of those was built as a pattern and then generalized to only a subset: code-splitting to 3 pages, background-poll suppression to 2 hooks, prefetch targets to 4 routes. One hand built the fast paths; the finishing pass that makes them the default across all ~40 surfaces was never taken, so cold-load ships a 2.5MB monolith and a hidden tab polls ~100 queries into the void.

synthesis.headline: Run 06's discovery is that run-05's arc pathology has graduated into systemic law: every truth mechanism the fleet lands is eroded by the next producer it never covered — 7 of 17 QC'd slices sit with-gaps for exactly that reason, including the flagship ouroboros fix, which a second ungated episode producer quietly reopened within days. Meanwhile the deepest deficit has moved inward and downward: the knowledge graph — the substrate every future JARVIS behavior depends on — is 89-99% untraceable with 40-75% of its remaining citations dangling, and the owner's daily chronicle is live-rendering raw LLM planning monologue as the owner's own briefing voice under a mismatched date. The program that follows is therefore one idea applied fifteen ways: stop fixing call sites and start shipping population-level coverage — ledgers, primitives, lints, and gates that the NEXT producer inherits by default.
